# What Supabase secret keys the library redacts, and what it leaves alone.
#
# Every key here is built from the ordered run 0123456789abcdef, which no real
# credential is: the random part is that run written once and then as far as 5,
# which is the twenty-two characters the generator slices out of a base64url
# encoding, and the checksum behind the separator is the first eight of the same
# run. It is not an abbreviation — a body shortened for readability would leave a
# case holding no key at all — and with the prefix in front a key comes to
# forty-one characters.
#
# The case about a body of underscores alone carries no ordered run. What it
# states is that the count either side of the separator is what divides the
# parts, and a body of one repeated character is what leaves nothing else to
# read the division by.

patterns: supabase-secret-key

# A key as it is written. A secret key bypasses row level security and stands
# for the whole of a project's data, so Supabase refuses one sent from a browser
# and what carries one is a server: its configuration, the header its requests
# send, and the response the Management API first reveals one in.

case:     a key in an environment assignment
in:       SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY=sb_secret_0123456789abcdef012345_01234567
out:      SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY=«supabase-secret-key»

case:     a key in an apikey header
in:       apikey: sb_secret_0123456789abcdef012345_01234567
out:      apikey: «supabase-secret-key»

case:     a key in a bearer token header
in:       Authorization: Bearer sb_secret_0123456789abcdef012345_01234567
out:      Authorization: Bearer «supabase-secret-key»

case:     a key in a curl invocation
in:       curl -H "apikey: sb_secret_0123456789abcdef012345_01234567" https://api.supabase.co/rest/v1/todos
out:      curl -H "apikey: «supabase-secret-key»" https://api.supabase.co/rest/v1/todos

case:     a key in the response that reveals it
in:       {"api_key":"sb_secret_0123456789abcdef012345_01234567","type":"secret"}
out:      {"api_key":"«supabase-secret-key»","type":"secret"}

case:     a key in a server side client constructor
in:       createClient(url, "sb_secret_0123456789abcdef012345_01234567")
out:      createClient(url, "«supabase-secret-key»")

case:     a key at the end of a sentence
in:       the key is sb_secret_0123456789abcdef012345_01234567.
out:      the key is «supabase-secret-key».

# The alphabet. A body is two slices of a base64url encoding, so both cases, the
# digits, the hyphen and the underscore are admitted throughout — the key the
# vendor's own tooling writes into a local stack carries a hyphen. What is not
# admitted is everything else: a dot, a space, or any character the encoding
# does not draw from ends the reading.

case:     an uppercase random part
in:       sb_secret_0123456789ABCDEF012345_01234567
out:      «supabase-secret-key»

case:     a hyphen in the random part
in:       sb_secret_0123456789-bcdef012345_01234567
out:      «supabase-secret-key»

case:     an underscore in the random part
in:       sb_secret_0123456789_bcdef012345_01234567
out:      «supabase-secret-key»

case:     a hyphen in the checksum
in:       sb_secret_0123456789abcdef012345_0123456-
out:      «supabase-secret-key»

case:     a dot in the random part
in:       sb_secret_0123456789.bcdef012345_01234567
out:      sb_secret_0123456789.bcdef012345_01234567

case:     a body broken by a space
in:       sb_secret_0123456789 bcdef012345_01234567
out:      sb_secret_0123456789 bcdef012345_01234567

# The separator, which is the tightening this pattern has and the rulesets
# written against this prefix do not. The generator writes an underscore between
# the twenty-two characters of randomness and the eight of checksum, so the
# twenty-third character of a body is the one position that may be nothing else.
# The alphabet holds the underscore, so it is the count either side of it that
# says where the parts divide — a body carrying underscores elsewhere is a key
# all the same, and one carrying none where the separator belongs is not.

case:     a body of underscores alone
in:       sb_secret________________________________
out:      «supabase-secret-key»

case:     a hyphen where the separator stands
in:       sb_secret_0123456789abcdef012345-01234567
out:      sb_secret_0123456789abcdef012345-01234567

case:     the separator one character early
in:       sb_secret_0123456789abcdef01234_501234567
out:      sb_secret_0123456789abcdef01234_501234567

case:     the separator one character late
in:       sb_secret_0123456789abcdef0123450_1234567
out:      sb_secret_0123456789abcdef0123450_1234567

case:     a body of the right length with no separator
in:       sb_secret_0123456789abcdef012345001234567
out:      sb_secret_0123456789abcdef012345001234567

# The lengths either side of the count. Twenty-two and eight are the two slices
# of the generator and are printed in the documentation's own prose, so the
# counts are read exactly rather than as the range two rulesets read: a body one
# character short is not a key, and a run one character longer is a key with a
# character left over.

case:     a body of thirty-one characters is a key
in:       sb_secret_0123456789abcdef012345_01234567
out:      «supabase-secret-key»

case:     a body one character short is not
in:       sb_secret_0123456789abcdef012345_0123456
out:      sb_secret_0123456789abcdef012345_0123456

case:     a body run one character longer is a key and the character after it
in:       sb_secret_0123456789abcdef012345_012345678
out:      «supabase-secret-key»8

# What a key may be written against. There is no boundary on either side of the
# prefix, so a key keeps its span whatever character it abuts, and what stands
# past the forty-first character stays where it was written. The tightening that
# would rule the first two out is the demand the Slack and Stripe patterns make,
# that no letter and no digit stand in front of a prefix. It is declined because
# the prefix is ten characters closing on an underscore, so no word is spelled
# with it at the end; what it would cost is the second case below, a key written
# straight against a letter, which would then be left in the text whole rather
# than trimmed.

case:     a key after an underscore
in:       SUPABASE_KEY_sb_secret_0123456789abcdef012345_01234567
out:      SUPABASE_KEY_«supabase-secret-key»

case:     a key after a letter
in:       xsb_secret_0123456789abcdef012345_01234567
out:      x«supabase-secret-key»

case:     a word written against a key
in:       sb_secret_0123456789abcdef012345_01234567suffix
out:      «supabase-secret-key»suffix

case:     a hyphenated word written against a key
in:       sb_secret_0123456789abcdef012345_01234567-suffix
out:      «supabase-secret-key»-suffix

# Keys written together, and the key written inside another. The alphabet a body
# is drawn from holds every character the prefix is written with, so a body may
# spell the prefix and open a candidate that reads on past the end of the key it
# stands in. That is why the scan resumes a byte past the start of a candidate
# rather than past the candidate, and the last case is what a scan stepping over
# what it declined would lose: the two spans overlap and are redacted as one.

case:     two keys with nothing between them
in:       sb_secret_0123456789abcdef012345_01234567sb_secret_0123456789abcdef012345_01234567
out:      «supabase-secret-key»«supabase-secret-key»

case:     two keys separated by a space
in:       sb_secret_0123456789abcdef012345_01234567 sb_secret_0123456789abcdef012345_01234567
out:      «supabase-secret-key» «supabase-secret-key»

case:     a prefix in front of a key
in:       sb_secret_sb_secret_0123456789abcdef012345_01234567
out:      sb_secret_«supabase-secret-key»

case:     a key beginning inside another
in:       sb_secret_sb_secret_0123456789ab_012345670_01234567
out:      «supabase-secret-key»

# A base64url run written behind the prefix, which is the collision this format
# leaves. Thirty-one characters of that alphabet with an underscore twenty-three
# characters in is the vendor's format exactly, so nothing is left in the text to
# tell such a run from a key — which is what the key in the first case of this
# file is written as — and declining it would decline every key Supabase issues.
#
# What has to be written to reach it is the literal prefix, ten characters
# carrying two underscores. Standard base64 writes no underscore at all, so a
# certificate, a PEM body or an embedded image holds no candidate at however
# long it runs.

case:     a base64url run behind the prefix
in:       sb_secret_0123456789abcdef012345_01234567
out:      «supabase-secret-key»

case:     a base64url run on its own
in:       0123456789abcdef012345_01234567
out:      0123456789abcdef012345_01234567

case:     a standard base64 payload
in:       payload=MIIBIjANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQEFAAOCAQ8AMIIBCgKCAQEAsbsecret
out:      payload=MIIBIjANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQEFAAOCAQ8AMIIBCgKCAQEAsbsecret

# And what this pattern leaves alone. First the prefix: the case the vendor
# writes it in, the underscore it closes with written as a hyphen and then left
# out. Then the publishable prefix, which is the same body behind a longer one
# and is what the pattern beside this reads. Then a body of the right shape with
# no prefix in front of it, and the prose and the log line no pattern here has
# anything to find in.

case:     an uppercase prefix
in:       SB_SECRET_0123456789abcdef012345_01234567
out:      SB_SECRET_0123456789abcdef012345_01234567

case:     a hyphen where the prefix carries its closing underscore
in:       sb_secret-0123456789abcdef012345_01234567
out:      sb_secret-0123456789abcdef012345_01234567

case:     the prefix without its closing underscore
in:       sb_secret0123456789abcdef012345_01234567
out:      sb_secret0123456789abcdef012345_01234567

case:     a publishable key
in:       sb_publishable_0123456789abcdef012345_01234567
out:      sb_publishable_0123456789abcdef012345_01234567

case:     a personal access token
in:       sbp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      sbp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     a body of the right shape opening with no prefix
in:       xxxxxxxxxx0123456789abcdef012345_01234567
out:      xxxxxxxxxx0123456789abcdef012345_01234567

case:     prose
in:       there is no credential in this sentence
out:      there is no credential in this sentence

case:     a log line
in:       time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="calling api" url=https://api.supabase.co/rest/v1/todos
out:      time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="calling api" url=https://api.supabase.co/rest/v1/todos
